expectations_used.implement: Delivers all three functions: an iterative flood fill that counts one zone per unvisited shelving cell, steps only in the four orthogonal directions, and marks visited outside the caller's grid so the plan comes back byte-identical; a binary search on rate bounded above by `max(loads)` whose feasibility check is one linear ceiling-sum pass with no per-rate list building; and an end-sorted prefix DP over the bookings that locates each predecessor by binary search rather than rescanning, on a copy so the caller's order is preserved — with the `ValueError` paths (ragged rows, zero-width rows, unknown cell symbol, empty `loads`, non-positive load, `shifts` below 1 or below the aisle count, a non-triple booking, `end <= start`, negative value) raised before any traversal, search or planning begins.
expectations_used.verify: Dry-runs before the one submission: re-reads each expectation against the code (does `count_zones([])` return 0 without falling into the width check; does the enclosed cell in the donut plan really get counted as its own zone; does `max_dock_value` treat `(0,3)` and `(3,6)` as compatible rather than clashing), confirms the three large tests pass on their own rather than assuming they will, and checks the whole 49-test suite green in one run rather than per-file.
